key_insight: The paper detects out-of-distribution inputs by testing how much a model’s prediction changes when its internal representation is perturbed along class-specific semantic concept directions.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trust and safety in medical imaging by flagging cases where a model may be confidently wrong on unfamiliar scans or conditions.
method: Learn sparse autoencoders from in-distribution data to extract class-specific concept vectors.
Perturb deeper-layer representations using the concept vector for the model’s predicted class.
Measure how stable the class logits remain; low stability suggests OOD input.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a representation-level OOD detection framework designed for medical imaging and evaluated by comparing prediction stability on in-distribution versus OOD samples.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the learned concepts capture true clinical semantics, and the approach may be sensitive to the chosen layer and perturbation design.
paper_title: When Confidence Lacks Concepts: Interpretable OOD Detection via Representation Perturbations
